methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Navier is a seed-stage transportation company that has raised $7.2M to date. The transportation sector comp universe includes six private peers—among them Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, EarthGrid, and Olympian Motors—and zero public comparables. A narrow peer-median approach proved infeasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints within transportation; three transportation peers exist broadly, but none met the threshold of three or more comparable transactions at equivalent valuation tiers.

Stage-progression analysis was the primary applicable method, using total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement. This approach yielded an implied valuation of $18M. Given the single-method constraint and inherent uncertainty in seed-stage progression multiples across transportation, a triangulated range of $15M (low) to $21M (high) frames the median estimate of $18M with a ±15% confidence band.

Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of a 2.5x multiplier for transportation-specific risk and the absence of direct peer benchmarking. The small raised capital base ($7.2M) and nascent stage limit visibility into unit economics or go-to-market traction. Any valuation within the $15–21M band remains contingent on validation of technology differentiation and capital efficiency metrics relative to the transportation peer set.
